items.title: Ammonium sulfate incorrectly resolves the source formula (NH4)2S4 as an exact synonym
items.body:
`data/ingredients/mapped/Nh42so4.yaml` carries `(NH4)2S4` as an active EXACT_SYNONYM of ammonium sulfate. This oxygen-free formula does not establish sulfate identity. The current `main` owner retrieved on 2026-11-08 has SHA256 `1806053b7d0adc25bd2d1a84f0aeae92185a69f84d2db46abe816c75c21db48d`, identical to the frozen campaign file.

The captured JCM response SHA256 is `63aa07eb253c6d8c98dd77996ece5ed908071ece832096f8a374f31f7b382795`.

Follow-up: retain the literal source text as provenance and quarantine this alias as REJECTED_LABEL on the sulfate owner. Keep the sulfate identity itself unchanged. The source case remains unresolved until provider clarification or reagent evidence distinguishes a source error from a different intended sulfur compound. Do not mint an exact sulfate association from lexical similarity or medium plausibility.

Worker03 has prepared a bounded isolated alias proposal, with primary follow-up and separate skeptical review, under `reports/all_unmatched_20261107/worker-03/chemicals/`. No maintained owner or export was edited. Guarded integration, fresh complete changed-owner review and the inherited native holds remain required.

Worker03 proposal `c-citric-monohydrate-boundary` retypes these three incompatible aliases as REJECTED_LABEL while retaining their provenance. Keep the genuine hydrate spellings and the existing monohydrate identity. Rejecting a mismatched source label does not assert that the culture contains no citrate anions after dissolution; it preserves the distinction between supplied substance and solution species.

This is an isolated proposal, not an applied curation change. Coordinator integration must synchronize SSSOM and re-review the changed owner under the current native holds before publishing it. Its retained chemistry also needs correction: the source describes a polymer, not a finite oligomer. The frozen campaign owner and live `main` file retrieved on 2026-11-08 have the same SHA256, `9e0e563c06141faa41510a655cc3e1821d7a225c09236b309e2a2c1d541b7848`.

The generic beta-polyhydroxybutyric-acid source label is a separate granularity: [ChEBI:53389](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/CHEBI:53389) represents the polymer without the R/S specification. These are coordinated proposals, not four independently applicable changes: verify both before hashes in each pair, retain source provenance, correct the molecular representation, and retire only the corresponding duplicate. The generic record's `Role:Carbon source` token is an annotation, not a resolving substance synonym.

No maintained records were changed. Complete changed-owner review, existing native holds, guarded integration and synchronized exports remain required. Evidence and exact payloads are retained under `reports/all_unmatched_20261107/worker-03/chemicals/`.

items.title: Pin the SSSOM invariants a sweep found already true, and unify object_source (#301, #385, #386, #504, #529)
items.body:
Closes #301. Closes #385. Closes #386. Closes #504. Closes #529.

A full-queue issue sweep measured five properties on the published set and found every one at zero. That is the cheapest moment to pin a property and the easiest moment to lose it — nothing was watching any of them, so a regression would ship silently and the next sweep would rediscover it from scratch.

## Three become invariants

| rule | property | issue |
|---|---|---|
| **G** | header `mapping_set_version` / `mapping_date` equal the newest row `mapping_date` | #301 |
| **H** | one published label belongs to one record | #504, #232 |
| **I** | `other` does not repeat a synonym, case-insensitively | #529 |

Rule G is anchored to the **data, not the clock**, so the file stays reproducible — checking against today's date is the defect kg-microbe fixed in its own artifact. Nothing bumped these fields, so they were hand-edited and wrong most of the time, and a version that does not move is worse than no version because a consumer reads it as "unchanged".

Rule H counts **distinct subjects**, never rows. A record legitimately publishes its ontology row plus registry identity rows — 2,999 rows over 2,624 subjects — so a row-count check would have flagged 257 correct records.

All three pass on the published set:

```
OK: ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv passed Rules A, B1, B2, B3, C, D, E, F, G, H, I.
```

## Two needed no rule

**#441** — a comma-stripped `object_label` is already refused by the id↔label gate, which carries `[object_id, object_label]` as a blocking pair under `canonical_or_synonym`. A digit-space-digit heuristic would only have added false positives on legitimate labels.

**#386** — detection is Rule C. What was missing was *prevention*.

## So object_source becomes one table (#385)

There were three: eleven prefixes in `reconcile_sssom`, eight in `promote_resolved_unmapped`, three registry prefixes in `reground_mapped_record`. The promotion table was missing `cas`, `kgmicrobe.compound`, `kgmicrobe.ingredient` — **682 of the 2,999 published rows, 23%** — and every writer looked the value up with `.get(prefix, "")`, so promoting to one of those wrote an empty column and nothing raised.

`object_source_for()` raises instead. Six writers now call it, and a test fails any writer that reintroduces the `.get(..., "")` shape.

## The tautology this uncovered

`PROMOTABLE` is now spelled out rather than derived from that table, because sharing the fuller one would silently add `cas:` and `kgmicrobe.*` as promotion destinations — a curation policy change. `--parent` must name an ontology term (MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md §3), and a registry `--to` is handled by the `is_registry_mint` branch, never this gate.

That broke `test_promotable_covers_every_published_object_source`:

```python
assert promote.PROMOTABLE == frozenset(promote.OBJECT_SOURCE)   # PROMOTABLE = frozenset(OBJECT_SOURCE)
```

A set compared to the thing it was derived from — it could not fail. Its docstring claimed to guarantee that every publishable prefix is reachable by promotion, and while it sat green the three registry prefixes were missing from that table entirely. **The tautology is what let #385 persist.** It now asserts the explicit set, and a second test checks the property the old one only claimed: every published prefix is reachable as an ontology destination *or* as a registry mint.

That is the same defect class as #591 last week — something shaped like a check, providing none.

## Verification

Rules G/H/I, the silent-lookup guard, and the replacement for the tautological test are all **mutation-checked** — each fails when the thing it guards is removed. Dropping `MESH` from `PROMOTABLE` produces `mesh is published but no promotion path reaches it`.

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `just qc-sssom` | passes A–I |
| `just lint` / `format-check` / `typecheck` | clean (38 files) |
| new tests | 39, plus 2 corrected |

Full suite was green at 2,079 passed before this fix and is re-running; I will confirm it before merging.

items.title: Rule F: reject a published row without a real mapping_date (#550)
items.body:
Fixes #550. Completes #542.

## The gap

culturebotai-claw#344 made the builder emit an **empty** `mapping_date` when a
record has no parseable `curation_history` timestamp, instead of inventing one
from the file's mtime. That was the honest half of the fix — but nothing
rejected the blank:

- `validate_sssom_invariants.py` never mentioned the column
- the shared contract in `kg_microbe_sssom` doesn't either
- the `sssom` package's JSON-schema validation **accepts** it — verified by
  blanking one on a real published row and running it clean

The builder's warning is one line in a log that runs to hundreds. A dateless
row would have shipped through every gate this repo has.

## Rule F

Every published row must carry `YYYY-MM-DD`. Offenders go to
`needs_curator_review.tsv` like the other rules, and `qc-sssom` exits 2.

The reasoning for making it a hard reject rather than a warning: a row without
a date cannot be ordered against its siblings or audited for staleness, and the
record behind it is missing the `curation_history` event `CLAUDE.md` requires
on every material change. That's a curation defect, so it belongs in the
curator's queue.

## Verified both directions on the live artifact

```
OK: ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv passed Rules A, B1, B2, B3, C, D, E, F.
```

Then, with two rows blanked:

```
row 2: MIM:~28-~29-quinic_Acid ... — mapping_date is empty for subject
  'MIM:~28-~29-quinic_Acid' — the record has no parseable curation_history
  timestamp, so the builder had no date to publish (#550)
error: recipe `qc-sssom` failed on line 95 with exit code 2
```

File restored afterwards; the rule passes clean again.

## Tests

`tests/test_sssom_mapping_date_gate.py`, 5 cases: dated rows pass; empty is
rejected and the reason names the subject and issue; four malformed shapes
(`2026-9-6`, `yesterday`, an ISO datetime, `20260906`) are rejected; whitespace
counts as empty; and one bad row among good ones is reported alone, at its
position.

The **101 existing tests** that load the validator still pass, and no test
asserted the old rule-summary string.

## Exposure today: zero

All 2,996 published rows are dated. This is preventive — it turns #542's
warning into a gate before the first record without history reaches it.

items.title: Rule G blocks ordinary curation: appending a row dated today fails qc-sssom with no one-step way to fix it
items.body:
Adversarial self-review of #601, which introduces Rule G.

Rule G requires the header's `mapping_set_version` / `mapping_date` to equal the newest row `mapping_date`. That is the right anchor — it makes the header move with the data instead of going quietly stale (#301) — but it converts a silent problem into a **blocking** one, and there is no single command that satisfies it.

Simulated a curator appending one row dated today and leaving the header alone:

```
$ validate_sssom_invariants.py <set with one row dated 2026-09-09>
exit=2
```

Every MIM-side row writer is affected — `promote_resolved_unmapped`, `promote_microbedecoder_reviewed`, `reground_mapped_record`, `relabel_mapped_record`, `merge_mapped_records`, `move_mapped_out_of_unmapped_collection` — because none of them touch the header. Only `reconcile_sssom` does:

```python
if ln.startswith("# mapping_set_version:"):
    ln = f'# mapping_set_version: "{date}"\n'
```

but that runs under `--apply`, whose job is reconciling STALE/ORPHAN rows, and it stamps whatever `--date` the operator passed — which can itself disagree with the newest row and leave Rule G red.

So today the only reliable way to satisfy a new blocking gate is to hand-edit the header, which is the very thing #301 says is unreliable.

This is the shape #484 warns about: a pin that taxes ordinary curation. A gate that is routinely red teaches people to ignore it.

items.title: Rule D: the identity row must be exactMatch, and republish (#438)
items.body:
Closes #438. Pairs with culturebotai-claw#119, which fixes the builder; this adds the assertion and republishes.

## Rule D

448 published rows said `skos:closeMatch` against the record's own `identifier` — *"this record is similar to itself"*. Rule D rejects any row whose `object_id` equals the subject record's `identifier` and whose predicate is not `skos:exactMatch`.

Strict from the start rather than report-then-enforce, because the builder fix takes the count to 0 in the same change.

The rule lives here because the builder lives in another repo and **only this file is gated by MIM's CI** — claw#119 stops it recurring, Rule D notices if it does anyway.

## A pre-existing bug found while wiring it

`_yaml_path_for_subject` mapped `MIM:<slug>` straight to `<slug>.yaml` with no unescaping, so it looked for `~28R~29-lactate.yaml` when the file is `(R)-lactate.yaml`.

**All 19 escaped subjects resolved to no file.** That silently disabled Rule A's registry-corroboration tier for them, and would have disabled Rule D entirely. #236's publish added 11 of the 19, so this got worse yesterday.

Now resolved through an index built **forwards** from the real filenames: the `~HEX` escape is variable-width (`~3911` is `chr(0x391) + "1"`, and nothing in the string says so) so decoding is ambiguous, but encoding each real stem is not.

## The republished artifact

```
rows 2885 -> 2885 | keys added 0 | removed 0
columns changed: {'predicate_id': 448}   all closeMatch -> exactMatch
```

Predicates now `exactMatch` 2649 / `narrowMatch` 142 / `closeMatch` 94.

items.title: Restore the CultureMech grounding evidence the residual importer never wrote (#541)

Fixes #541.

## Root cause

110 records created from CultureMech's unresolved residual in #505 carried their
provenance **only in the published SSSOM, never in the records**.

`create_records_from_groundings.py` emitted those rows directly, stamping
`MIM:culturemech:output/ingredient_occurrences.tsv` into `source`. It never wrote
the matching `ontology_mapping.evidence`. The builder derives `source` solely
from `ontology_mapping.evidence[].source`
(`build_mim_ingredient_sssom.py::_join_sources`), so the tag was an artifact-only
value that no rebuild could reproduce. #540 rebuilt honestly from the records,
and all 110 rows lost it.

The two sets coincide **exactly**, which is what identified the cause rather than
merely correlating with it:

```
mapped records with no ontology_mapping.evidence : 110
subjects that lost the tag in #540               : 110
overlap                                          : 110
tagged but has evidence                          :   0
no-evidence but never tagged                     :   0
```

## The fix invents nothing

Every affected record already states its origin in `curation_history` — action
`CREATED_FROM_CULTUREMECH_RESIDUAL`, curator
`claude_culturemech_residual_grounding`, and a `changes` line naming both the
ontology match and the occurrence table:

> Grounded to CHEBI:28854 ('2,4-D') on an exact match of an exact synonym to the
> query '2,4-Dichlorophenoxyacetic acid'. Source:
> culturemech:output/ingredient_occurrences.tsv.

`scripts/restore_culturemech_grounding_evidence.py` promotes that narrative into
the structured field the builder reads. A record is touched **only** where its
own history attests the origin — the dry run skipped **0** for missing
provenance.

The restored note distinguishes a label hit from a synonym hit by reading the
importer's own sentence, yielding **63 label / 47 synonym** — which matches the

items.title: Merge the aldehydo- duplicate pairs onto the class term (#398)
items.body:
Closes #398. Depends on `supplied_form` from #402 (merged).

```
n-Acetyl-muramic acid  CHEBI:47966 aldehydo-  ->  N-acetylmuramic acid  CHEBI:47965  occ 11
D-(-)-lyxose           CHEBI:16789 aldehydo-  ->  D-lyxose              CHEBI:62318  occ  0
```

Both pairs were **one substance recorded twice**, split across a ChEBI class term and its open-chain form — the muramic pair carried an identical CAS *and* formula on both records.

## This reverses the recommendation I gave earlier

ChEBI hangs the **commercial** CAS on the `aldehydo-` form in both cases (10597-89-4, 1114-34-7) while the class terms carry a different CAS or none. Reading the orderability rule off that alone, I recommended merging **into** the `aldehydo-` terms.

I was contorting identity to preserve CAS fidelity because there was nowhere else to put the CAS. #402 gave it somewhere:

- the purchasable CAS goes in **`supplied_form`** on the survivor, noting it is the CAS ChEBI attaches to the open-chain form;
- **`publish_cas_as_synonym.py` republishes it as a synonym**, so both nodes now carry `CAS:10597-89-4` / `CAS:1114-34-7` in the SSSOM `other` column and therefore in KGX.

Nothing purchasable is lost from the identity — it simply stopped having to ride on it.

items.title: Recover 187 surface forms a shadowed loop variable dropped; make PREDICATE a rule (#523, #525)
items.body:
Closes #523 and #525.

## #523 was filed on a false premise; this is the actual cause

I reported "19 SSSOM subjects have no record file after renames, stranding 1,409 tokens."
**There were never any stale subjects.** Checked directly against the escaped CURIEs,
every published subject resolves to a record file.

The real cause was a variable-shadowing bug in the backfill merged as #522. Inside the
token loop:

```python
key = token.casefold()          # rebinds the loop's (subject_id, object_id) tuple
```

From the second token in a row onward, `records.get(key[0])` looked up the token's first
**character**, found nothing, and counted it as "no matching record". Each row migrated
its first surface form and silently dropped the rest.

It produced no error and no wrong data — only under-application — and was invisible
except as an implausible statistic: `no_record` reported 1,364 for a corpus whose true
answer is 0. That is the kind of number worth disbelieving.

**Recovered: 187 surface forms across 62 records** that #522 should have migrated.
The other 1,419 are correctly skipped — names another record already publishes, caught by
the ambiguity guard.

Index effect: **+182 rows, all `unique`, conflicts unchanged at 468.**

## #525: the sweep found the same defect one table over

`PREDICATE` enumerated five grades; the corpus uses nine. `PLACEHOLDER`,
`CAS_RN_LOOKUP`, `LEXICAL_MATCH` and `BROAD_MATCH` — **339 records** — raised `KeyError`
on every write path that indexed it, and **four scripts index it**. A `KeyError` on a
write path is a row that never gets written, so this stayed silent until someone promoted
a record with one of those grades.

Now a rule mirroring the builder: `exactMatch` by default, `closeMatch` for any non-exact
quality so consumers don't read it as identity, `narrowMatch` for `NARROW_MATCH`.

**It reproduces the old table exactly for all five grades it covered** — the published
SSSOM is byte-identical after the rewiring — and it fails weak, so an unrecognised grade
gets `closeMatch` rather than asserting an identity nobody curated.

The generalisation in #525 holds: any lookup keyed on one of MIM's warn-only
organically-growing enums has this shape, because the enum grows and the table doesn't.

## Tests

A source-level guard for the shadowing (a behavioural test would need the full corpus
plus a kg-microbe checkout; the defect is one rebinding, so asserting it can't return is
cheaper and more direct), plus the CURIE round-trip, the damage triage — including the
two conventions that are **not** damage, ChEBI's `<compound>--water (1/n)` hydrates and
CAS inverted nomenclature — and a test that walks every `mapping_quality` in the corpus
and asserts it resolves. That last one is the check that would have caught both KeyErrors.

## Verification

1,515 tests · `validate-strict` 0 errors · SSSOM Rules A/B1/B2/B3/C/D/E ·
`reconcile_sssom` GAP/ORPHAN/STALE 0 · duplicate identifiers match the baseline ·
`qc-roundtrip` verified · mypy and ruff clean.

items.title: One rule for SSSOM confidence and justification, mirroring the builder (#519)
items.body:
Closes #519.

## The defect

Two things write `confidence` and `mapping_justification`: MIM's promotion helpers and
claw's `build_mim_ingredient_sssom.py`. They disagreed, so whichever ran last won and the
values flipped across rebuilds. Measured on one promotion whose diff otherwise showed
**zero identity changes**:

```
confidence            0.99 -> 0.9   205   (all CAS_RN_LOOKUP records)
                      0.95 -> 0.99   49   (all SYNONYM_MATCH records)
mapping_justification LexicalMatching -> ManualMappingCuration   124
                      ManualMappingCuration -> LexicalMatching    65
```

## The fix

`mediaingredientmech.sssom_grading` holds the rule, mirroring claw's — because **claw is
the generator**. It rebuilds every row from the records, so a value MIM writes that
disagrees survives only until the next build. Mirroring makes a rebuild a no-op instead
of a rewrite.

Two rules, and why they are what they are:

- **`SYNONYM_MATCH` is 0.99, not 0.95.** The schema glosses it *"Matches known synonym in
  ontology"*, which says how the term was **located**, not that the identity is
  approximate — `CLOSE_MATCH` is the value reserved for that. The row already carries
  `skos:exactMatch`, so grading it below a label match contradicted its own predicate.
- **Justification is derived, not asserted.** MIM's writers hardcoded
  `ManualMappingCuration`, which described 107 records created by exact string matching as
  hand-curated. A registry-mint sibling row deliberately stays manual: minting is a
  curator deciding no ontology term fits, which is the opposite of a lexical match.

## A third table nobody had noticed

`promote_microbedecoder_residual.py` carried its own **three-grade** copy — missing
`NARROW_MATCH` and `FALLBACK_REGISTRY`, so those raised `KeyError` rather than writing a
row. The other three writers already imported from `promote_resolved_unmapped` (the #279
pattern), so this leaves MIM with one table instead of three.

## Keeping it in step

`tests/test_sssom_grading.py` parses claw's own constants at the sibling path and skips
when claw is absent — the same shape as the SSSOM validator's Rule B4. Verified
non-vacuous: it compares parsed sets, so dropping `SYNONYM_MATCH` on either side fails it.

Full vendoring through `scripts/.vendored_canon_ref` would be stronger, but needs a claw
PR merged first; this closes the drift now and the test names claw as the authority.

## Realigning what was already written

`regrade_sssom_columns.py` fixes the 443 cells written before the rule existed, using a
fresh build as the reference and touching only those two columns.

**Identity is provably untouched**: keys identical, zero `predicate_id` or `object_label`
changes, and the only columns that differ are the two named.

The publish diff now reports neither — `confidence` and `mapping_justification` have
dropped out of it entirely:

```
same key + predicate  2995      added 0 · removed 0 · re-spelled 0 · flipped 0
Other columns changed: other 1662 · source 1245 · mapping_date 1216 · validation_method 155
```

## Verification

1,484 tests · SSSOM Rules A/B1/B2/B3/C/D/E · `reconcile_sssom` GAP/ORPHAN/STALE 0.

items.title: Move the SSSOM surface forms only MIM knows onto the records (#520)
items.body:
Implements the decision recorded on #520: **ontology synonyms are curated onto records,
not emitted by the builder.**

## Why not the builder

kg-microbe transforms ChEBI itself — 158,214 of 200,000 sampled nodes carry synonyms —
and for `CHEBI:16004` its node holds a **superset** of MIM's row. So **7,713** of the
tokens a rebuild drops are a second, stale copy of data the consumer already has.
Emitting them from the builder would institutionalise that redundancy and leave MIM
shipping a ChEBI snapshot it cannot keep current.

MIM's unique contribution is the surface forms no ontology has (`n-propyl chloride`,
`1,2-propandiol`). **Only MIM sees the recipes**, so only a record can hold them. The
curation layer already assumes this — the builder honours
`NON_PUBLISHABLE_MIM_SYNONYM_TYPES = {"REJECTED_LABEL"}`, which only makes sense if
records are the source.

## What this lands

**114 surface forms onto 114 records** as `RAW_TEXT` (raw forms from an artifact whose
per-token provenance can't be verified; `EXACT_SYNONYM` would overstate them).

Effect on the published index: **+103 rows, all `unique`, conflicts unchanged at 468.**

## The guard is the point, and the first cut didn't have it

Adding a synonym is only safe if no *other* record already answers to that name.
`label_index.csv` is what CultureMech resolves against and it **fails closed** on a name
two records claim. Many ontology synonyms are legitimately shared across a family —
`L-aspartic acid` belongs to the acid, its potassium salt and its sodium salt alike.

Migrating 1,713 tokens without that check measured as:

| | unique | conflict:different_substances |
|---|---:|---:|
| `origin/main` | 8,758 | 468 |
| unguarded backfill | **8,271** | **1,921** |
| this PR | **8,861** | **468** |

The unguarded version would have made ~487 previously resolvable labels **unresolvable** —
strictly worse than the missing synonyms it set out to fix. 195 tokens are now skipped on
those grounds.

## Also deliberately not migrated

- **20 damaged forms whose repair reproduces a name already published.** `L--Aspartic
  acid`, `2--Mercaptoethanol`, `myo--Inositol` all collapse onto names the record *and*
  the kg-microbe node already carry, so they add nothing. Repair-then-retest is what
  shows this; a blanket drop was right for them only by accident.
- **6 role-text leaks** (`utilizes: 1,2-propandiol`, `carbon source: acetate`) — defects
  sitting in the published artifact, not synonyms.
- **1 truncated inside a parenthetical** — unrepairable without fabricating text.
  Unbalanced parentheses are the test.
- **1,409 tokens on 19 subjects whose record was renamed after publication** — filed as
  #523; they cannot be attributed to a current record.

## Two survivors were never damaged

`beta-D-glucopyranose, 4-O-beta-D-galactopyranosyl-` is CAS index nomenclature ending on
the substituent's hyphen, and ChEBI writes hydrates as `<compound>--water (1/n)`. My
first damage filter read both as truncation and discarded valid labels for the citrate,
cobalt-sulfate and phosphate hydrates.

## Verification

1,470 tests · `validate-strict` 0 errors · SSSOM Rules A/B1/B2/B3/C/D/E ·
`reconcile_sssom` GAP/ORPHAN/STALE 0 · duplicate identifiers match the baseline ·
`qc-roundtrip` verified.

Requires kg-microbe's `data/transformed/ontologies`; the tool fails closed without them,
since otherwise every token looks unique and it would copy ChEBI wholesale into records.

items.title: #322: measure the cohort — the premise does not hold
items.body:
Advances #322. Does not close it — see "what remains" below.

## The premise did not survive measurement

#322 reads *"145 records map to structureless CHEBI class terms; 117 graded EXACT_MATCH"*. I partitioned the current 119-row cohort using the repo's **own** class-level heuristic — `DEFAULT_SUBCLASS_ALARM = 50`, from #203, via the bulk subclass-count index in `promote_microbedecoder_reviewed.py`.

**"No molecular formula" does not mean "class term."**

| direct subclasses of the CHEBI target | rows |
|---|---:|
| 0 — leaf | 44 |
| 1–4 — near-leaf | 46 |
| 5–49 — grouping | 21 |
| **≥50 — class** | **8** |

**90 of 119 targets have fewer than 5 subclasses.** They are leaves; the absent formula reflects polymers, dyes and salts whose chemistry was never backfilled — `Neutral red`, `1,1,2,2-Tetrachloroethane`, `Poly-beta-hydroxyalkanoate`.

**And where the target *is* a class, the MIM record names that same class** — every one of the 8:

```
Amino Acid          -> amino acid           (57 subclasses)
Bile Acid           -> bile acid           (415)
Hopanoid            -> hopanoid             (93)
Lactone             -> lactone             (164)
Macrolide Antibiotic-> macrolide antibiotic (68)
Hydrocarbon         -> hydrocarbon         (107)
Lipopolysaccharide  -> lipopolysaccharide  (134)
Polysaccharides     -> polysaccharide     (1677)
```

Class-to-class is legitimate. The defect #322 describes is a **specific substance** equated with a class, and none of these is that.

Of the 16 rows whose labels genuinely differ, 15 are spelling or synonym variants: `Gelatine`→`gelatin`, `MgCO3`→`magnesium carbonate`, `HEPES`→its systematic name, `Gentamicin`→`gentamycin`, `Benzylcyanide`→`phenylacetonitrile`, `Dihydrocelastrol`→`triptohypol C` (which lists `dihydrocelastrol` as a synonym).

## The one genuine defect, fixed

```
Carboxymethyl cellulose                CHEBI:234035   carboxymethylcellulose SODIUM SALT
Carboxymethyl cellulose (sodium salt)  FOODON:03460374
```

The generic record held the **salt's** term while the salt record held a FOODON term — crossed. Regrounded to `CHEBI:85146 "carboxymethylcellulose"`, the plain form, which lists **"Carboxymethyl cellulose"** among its synonyms: this record's label exactly.

It mattered downstream too. kg-microbe overwrites an ontology term's canonical name from a symmetric row, so the old mapping was renaming the *sodium salt* term to the generic name as well as asserting the wrong identity.

## What remains for #322

The issue should probably be **rescoped rather than closed**. If there is class-level overstatement in this corpus it is not in the formula-free `exactMatch` rows, and finding it needs a signal that compares what the *record* denotes against what the *term* denotes — the label-agreement test used here is a start, but it only catches cases where someone wrote a different name.

Noted, not changed: `Carboxymethyl cellulose (sodium salt)` sits on FOODON while `CHEBI:753907 "carboxymethylcellulose sodium"` exists. That is a FOODON-vs-CHEBI decision for salts, and #330 already has that record open on a different question.

items.title: Orderability decides granularity; settle #394 by it
items.body:
Closes #394. Records the design stance agreed 2026-08-18.

## The rule

> MIM is **practically oriented**: an ingredient record denotes **a specific chemical someone can order**. Where sources disagree about which form a recipe means, pick one by convention rather than splitting the record or retreating to a generic term. The operative test is **the CAS a lab would buy**.

Documented in `MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` §3, the `map-media-ingredients` skill (where curators meet it), and the README's design stance.

**Two limits stated with it**, because it is easy to over-apply:

- It does **not** merge things bought from different catalogue lines. A hydrate and its anhydrous form have different CAS numbers and formula weights and stay separate records. Orderability breaks ties about *which term names one purchasable thing*, not about whether two things are one.
- It **never discards detail**. Conflating concerns the record's *identity*; every raw form stays a synonym, so `label_index` keeps answering for all of them.

## #394, settled

Codex read the four source strings behind this record's occurrences, and they are genuinely mixed:

| medium | raw string |
|---|---|
| KOMODO 1111 | `Carboxymethyl cellulose` |
| DSMZ 1111 | `Carboxymethyl cellulose` (prep note: *"…sodium salt, high viscosity (Sigma No. C-5013)"*) |
| JCM 1052 | `Carboxymethyl cellulose, sodium salt` |
| DSMZ 1684 | `Carboxymethylcellulose (CMC), sodium salt` |

2 plain, 2 explicitly sodium salt. CultureBotHT's `compounds_to_cas.csv` already maps **both** the plain and the sodium name to the same CAS 9004-32-4, so the conflation predates MIM.

Under the rule the record stays on **CHEBI:234035**, which carries `cas:9004-32-4` — the product on the shelf. The plain term **CHEBI:85146** carries `cas:9000-11-7`, a different purchase.

**This vindicates the revert in #393.** I had regrounded this record to CHEBI:85146 on the strength of its label; that would have moved it to a different orderable substance. The record's own CAS was the evidence I skipped, and reverting rather than defending it was right.

`Carboxymethyl cellulose (sodium salt)` (FOODON:03460374, 0 occurrences) merges in — the two were crossed, the generic-looking record holding the salt's term while the salt-labelled record held a FOODON term.

## A dangling alias the merge created, caught by tests

`test_alias_map_targets_are_all_live` failed: `mim_curie_aliases.tsv` carried a rename pointing at `MIM:Carboxymethyl_Cellulose_Sodium_Salt`, which no longer exists. Repointed to the survivor **and** added an alias for the merged subject itself, so both the old percent-encoded CURIE and the merged one still resolve — the tombstone principle applied to subjects rather than identifiers.

## Verification

- `reconcile_sssom` in sync; invariants pass Rules A, B1, B2, B3, C

items.title: Fix a spelling that kg-microbe publishes as a ChEBI term's name
items.body:
Follow-up to the SSSOM delivery review (#392). Files #396.

## Why a spelling is now a delivery defect

kg-microbe's consolidator, for every symmetric row:

```python
self.add_chemical(id=object_id, canonical_name=subject_label, ...)
# MIM is the canonical-naming authority — force overwrite
self.chemicals[object_id]["canonical_name"] = subject_label
```

The entity is keyed by `object_id`, so **the node being renamed is the ontology term**; MIM's subject appears only as an xref. A misspelling in a MIM `preferred_term` therefore becomes the KG's name for a real ChEBI term.

```
1-Naphtylacetic Acid  ->  renames CHEBI:32918 '1-naphthaleneacetic acid'
```

`Naphtyl` should be `Naphthyl`. **This is not a regrounding** — the record stays on CHEBI:32918, denotes the same substance, and already carried `1-naphthylacetic acid` as a synonym, so the correct spelling was never in doubt.

The raw misspelling is kept as a `RAW_TEXT` synonym. `MAPPING_SEMANTICS` warns that renaming a record removes the raw label consumers match on; keeping it as a synonym is what avoids that, and `label_index` still resolves the original string.

**No kg-microbe change is needed.** The consolidator re-reads MIM on every run and the overwrite is forced so a fresher MIM run wins, so this propagates on the next consolidation.

## The subject id deliberately keeps the old spelling

The per-record filename was **not** renamed — `collect_existing_filenames` keeps the existing stem — so the SSSOM subject stays `MIM:1-naphtylacetic_Acid`. That is the #236-aware behaviour: a stable subject matters more than a tidy one, and re-deriving it from the new label is the mistake #293/#307 record. The replacement row was written by hand because `reconcile_sssom` correctly refuses to invent provenance for a new row.

## Scope: 3 rows, not the 5 I first counted

My first sweep flagged 5 "damaged" labels. **Two do not rename anything.** `MES Hydrat` maps symmetrically to `cas:145224-94-8` and `kgmicrobe.compound:mes_hydrat`, whose object labels are identical to it, and its `CHEBI:39005` row is a **narrowMatch** — asymmetric, so the ontology label is kept and MIM's term added as a synonym. The hydrate/anhydrous relationship there is modelled correctly. I had counted it by scanning all symmetric rows rather than only renaming ones.

The two left unfixed are deliberate, and filed as #396:

- **`(2)-D-lyxose`** → CHEBI:62318. The `(2)` is a mangled character from the microbedecoder ingest (`source_id=kgmicrobe.trait:2_d_lyxose`). I cannot tell what it was, and inventing a stereo descriptor is worse than leaving a visibly broken one.
- **`1,3-Butandiol`** → CHEBI:52683. `Butandiol` is correct **German**, not a typo, and the record came from a CAS lookup (107-88-0) that is chemically right. Whether MIM should carry an English label so an English-language KG gets one is a judgement about the delivery contract, not a defect. Only 1 of 835 renames is German, so the cost is trivial — but the rule governs every future label.

- `reconcile_sssom` in sync; invariants pass Rules A, B1, B2, B3, C
- filename case clean; `validate-all` 0 errors

items.title: Merge six identifier collisions, and gate the rest (#414)
items.body:
**32** ontology CURIEs were held by two or more LIVE records. In MIM a mapped record's `identifier` **is** its ontology CURIE, so that asserts two different ingredients are the same thing — the `Butane-1,4-diol` defect, generalised.

## The obvious rule is wrong here

"Merge when CAS and molecular formula agree" marks **22 of the 32** mergeable, and is wrong about most of them:

```
cas:9036-88-8    b-Mannan carob seed / Mannan from S. cerevisiae   different organisms
cas:84082-64-4   Mucin porcine stomach Type II / type III          different products
cas:39280-21-2   Rhamnogalacturonan: soy bean / potato             different sources
FOODON:03315719  Casein peptone / Casamino acids                   peptone vs acid hydrolysate
CHEBI:30769      Citric acid / Citric Acid·H2O                     anhydrous vs monohydrate
```

They agree on chemistry because the same CAS was **copied onto both records**, or the hydrate's properties were filled in from the anhydrous form. The test reproduces the very error it is asked to detect.

The **inverse** is sound, and is what protects the hydrate families (`CuSO4`/`x 2 H2O`/`x 4 H2O`, `FeSO4`/`x 5 H2O`/`x 6 H2O`): where formulas differ, the records certainly are not mergeable. Those need re-grounding, not merging.

So the six were chosen **by hand**, each carrying its reason in the script — pure notation, abbreviation or brand variants. **32 → 26.**

## A correction to the issue

#414 said 30. It is **32**: that filter required *every* record on an identifier to be live, so a group of two live records *plus a tombstone* was skipped. Corrected on the issue.

## This also fixes the half of #407 the dedupe could not reach

**30 graph nodes displayed a REJECTED label while the surviving record never appeared.** Dropping duplicate *nodes* could not fix it — `generate_ingredient_umap.py` indexes records **by identifier** and kept whichever globbed first, so by the time dedupe ran, both copies were the tombstone. Live records now win the index. **30 → 7**, and the remaining 7 are retired non-ingredients that are the *sole* holder of their identifier.

## Both stores are written, deliberately not via the export

MIM keeps every record twice — the curated aggregate and a per-record file under `data/ingredients/mapped/`. Earlier merge scripts wrote **only the aggregate**, leaving the per-record copy to a later export. That is precisely why the visualiser kept drawing merged-away labels: it reads the per-record files. I write both surgically for the 12 affected records, rather than invoke the `export-individual`/`aggregate-collections` pairing that #148 found silently reverted 55 curation events.

## The gate

`tests/test_identifier_uniqueness.py` fails on any collision **not** in an explicit allow-list, so a new one fails immediately while the 26 known ones stay enumerated with *why* each is open — split into hydrate families (re-ground), distinct products under one term (re-ground or mint), and brand-vs-generic (mergeable, but the brand may be worth keeping).

An allow-list rather than a threshold: a bare count lets one collision be repaired and another introduced in the same PR with no net change and no failure. A third test fails if an allow-list entry **stops** being a real collision, so the list cannot rot into describing a repo that no longer exists.

**Mutation-tested:** pointing a live record at another live record's CURIE takes it from 3 passed to 2 failed.

## Verified

- SSSOM Rules A/B1/B2/B3/C pass; visualization currency gate passes
- **950 tests** (947 base + 3 new)
- collisions 32 → 26; tombstone-labelled nodes 30 → 7; duplicate node ids 0

items.title: Near-match review report for the residual, and three exact-match defects it found
items.body:
Replaces #509, which GitHub auto-closed when #505 merged and its base branch was
deleted. Rebased onto main; the SSSOM rows were re-emitted rather than merged at their
old positions, because main now carries the row re-placement from #510.

## What this is

#505 grounds only *exact* matches, because a wrong grounding is worse than an honest
UNMAPPED. That deliberately leaves ~1,180 CultureMech surface forms with no proposal at
all. Many are close to a real term and a curator could settle them in seconds — but
"close" is exactly where the dangerous mistakes live. So this **reports and never
applies**.

`reports/culturemech_residual_near_matches.tsv`: **246 labels with a candidate, 418
candidate rows.**

## The similarity score is the least useful column

`H3BO4` against `H3BO3` scores 0.9+ similar and is a different species. No threshold
separates those. So the value is the `risks` column, which names *what differs*:

| flag | rows | why it matters |
|---|---:|---|
| TOKEN_DIFFERENCE | 196 | plain extra/missing words — the residual category |
| CONCENTRATION | 101 | a percentage or molarity survived the comparison |
| SALT_OR_ION_FORM | 91 | `Sodium glycerophosphate` vs `glycerophosphate` — different formula weight |
| PHYSICAL_STATE | 40 | `N2 gas` vs `dinitrogen` |
| STEREOCHEMISTRY | 23 | a racemate is not the stereo-unspecified parent |
| HYDRATION_STATE | 23 | 246.47 vs 120.37 g/mol (MAPPING_SEMANTICS §3) |
| NONE | 6 | nothing chemical differs — the safest rows |

A row flagged HYDRATION_STATE or FORMULA_DIGITS should be assumed wrong until confirmed.
A row with no flag differs only in spelling or word order.

## Candidate generation could not be a whole-string search

`DI Water` and `N2 gas` return nothing from oaklib — `is_partial` and `is_fuzzy`
included — because they are not substrings of any ontology label. It searches the
informative tokens instead (dropping presentation words; searching `solution` returns
thousands of unrelated terms) and scores candidates against the full label afterwards.

Formula expansion reaches what no string measure can: `N2 gas` and `dinitrogen` share
almost no characters. MIM's formula table had 19 entries and **not one gas**, while
`N2 gas` (71 mentions) and `Oxygen gas` (42) head the residual — so the 11 common gases
and water are added, each verified to expand to the actual CHEBI label.

## Three defects the report found in the exact-match pass

This is the part worth reviewing. **The report's own output found bugs in #505's pass.**

1. **oaklib's search is case-sensitive by default.** The report surfaced
   `Sodium glycerophosphate` → NCIT:C120561 at similarity **1.000 with no risk flags** —
   which is what an exact match looks like when the exact pass has missed one. The
   lowercase normalised query never reached the capitalised label. Re-running the pass
   over all 1,185 unmatched labels with `force_case_insensitive=True` recovered 6.
2. **Greek letters never matched anything.** Of 418 candidate rows only six carried no
   risk flag, and all six were Greek-letter labels beside the term they obviously denote.
   CHEBI stores `beta-D-glucose`; recipe text writes `β-D-glucose`. `beta-NAD` resolves
   to CHEBI:15846 and `β-NAD` resolved to *nothing whatsoever*.
3. **Micro-prefixed concentrations were never stripped.** The branch matched mg/l and w/v
   but not `µg/µL`, so `Biotin (1 µg/µL)` could not reach `Biotin`. Six vitamin records
   were held up by that alone.

All three are fixed here, and all of them turned out to be ALIAS cases — MIM already held
every one of those records; only the spelling was missing.

## Applied

3 new records (`Sodium glycerophosphate` NCIT:C120561, `Dichloran` CHEBI:27864, 
`hydroxocobalamin hydrochloride` NCIT:C217966) and 12 synonyms.

**One proposal excluded by judgement, not by a guard**: `Vitamin supplement (ATCC)` →
NCIT:C210732 `Vitamin Supplement`. Stripping the vendor tag makes the strings equal, but
a proprietary undefined mixture is not the generic class — a broadMatch wearing an exact
match's clothes.

## Cumulative (on top of #505, now merged)

**443 labels / 1,466 recipe mentions (24% of the unresolved mass) now resolve literally**,
up from 154/1,180 at `origin/main`. Index 8,367 → 8,843 rows.

## Verification

1,447 tests · `validate-strict` 0 errors · SSSOM Rules A/B1/B2/B3/C/D/E ·
`reconcile_sssom` GAP/ORPHAN/STALE 0 · `qc-roundtrip` verified.

items.title: 30 ontology CURIEs are held by two or more LIVE records, which MIM's own rule forbids
items.body:
Found while fixing #407. That issue is a rendering defect; this is the data defect underneath it, and it is the more serious of the two.

In MIM a mapped record's `identifier` **is** its ontology CURIE. Two live records on the same CURIE therefore assert that two different ingredients are the same thing — the `Butane-1,4-diol` lesson, generalised.

Counting identifiers held by more than one record in the curated collections:

| shape | count | verdict |
|---|---:|---|
| MAPPED + REJECTED | 47 | **correct** — the merge-tombstone pattern; a tombstone deliberately carries the winner's identifier |
| **MAPPED + MAPPED** | **30** | **defect** |

The 30 split into two quite different problems, and they need opposite fixes.

**Genuine duplicates that should be merged:**

```
MICRO:0000182   'Bacto-tryptone' / 'Tryptone' (6 occ) / 'Tryptone peptone'
MICRO:0000178   'Bacto peptone' / 'Peptone'
MICRO:0000193   'Bacto brain heart infusion' / 'Brain heart infusion' / 'Brain heart infusion broth'
CHEBI:3312      'CaCl2' (502 occ) / 'Calcium Chloride' (15 occ)
CHEBI:86158     'CaCl22H2O' (2) / 'CaCl2 x 2 H2O' (4,343)
ENVO:00002263   'Garden soil' / 'air-dried garden soil'
```

These are notation or branding variants of one substance. Standard merge: keep the higher-occurrence label, fold the other in as a `RAW_TEXT` synonym.

**Distinct substances wrongly sharing one identifier** — these must NOT be merged:

```
CHEBI:31346     'CaSO4' (9)          vs 'CaSO4 x 7 H2O' (2)
CHEBI:30769     'Citric acid' (63)   vs 'Citric Acid•H2O' (3)
FOODON:03315719 'Casein peptone'     vs 'Casamino acids' (395)
MICRO:0000455   'Algal Trace Elements Solution' vs 'WC Trace Elements Solution'
```

An anhydrous salt and its heptahydrate have different CAS numbers, different formula weights and are ordered separately — `MAPPING_SEMANTICS` §"map to what you can order" is explicit that the orderability rule does **not** license collapsing them. One of each pair needs re-grounding to its own term, or a `kgmicrobe.compound:` mint where no term exists.

## Why nothing caught it

`validate_sssom_invariants.py` checks Rules A/B1/B2/B3/C over the SSSOM, none of which constrain identifier uniqueness among live records. The visualisation gate added in #405 checks that every published node names a record that exists — the converse. So an identifier can be issued twice and every gate stays green.

Worth a uniqueness gate once the 30 are triaged: live records must hold distinct identifiers, with tombstones explicitly exempt. Filing the count now so it cannot grow unnoticed while the triage waits.

items.title: Settle #236 and publish the rebuilt SSSOM
items.body:
Publishes `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv` for the first time since 2026-08-20, and settles the decision that was blocking it.

**Depends on culturebotai-claw#111** (the set-diff guard) for the diagnosis, though not for the artifact.

## The decision

**#236: `MIM:` subjects are derived from the ingredient YAML's filename stem** — which is what `CURIE_STANDARD.md` §1 has always documented: *"The SSSOM subject is derived from the ingredient YAML's filename stem … Filenames move … 113 changed a CURIE and are published as aliases."* Subjects are expected to move; the alias map is the mechanism.

#299 had reverted 64 such moves, but its stated objection was not the principle — it was that the renames *"produced no alias trail … which would have left all 64 dangling."* Commit 1 supplies the trail.

## What changed in the artifact — 2,938 → 2,885 rows

```
same key + predicate 2783 | added 20 | removed 73 | re-spelled 82 | flipped 0
```

**`same key + predicate` is not `identical row`.** Of those 2,783, roughly 1,900 differ in some other column: `source` 1886, `mapping_date` 1626, `other` 682, `mapping_justification` 203 (179 `LexicalMatching` → `ManualMappingCuration`), `confidence` 154, `object_label` 1. Most is legitimate rebuild output. The one `object_label` change is a regression to a comma-stripped form and is filed as #441 — it is 1 row, and its fix belongs in the record's `preferred_term` (#308/#313), not here. The guard's blindness to all of this is culturebotai-claw#115, fixed there.

**82 subjects re-spelled.** All resolve through `mim_curie_aliases.tsv`. 11 had subjects violating `curie.py`'s own `_CURIE_RE` (unescaped parens — `MIM:(R)-lactate`); **now 0**.

**73 rows removed, 67 of one shape** — `kgmicrobe.compound:` registry rows on `cas:`-primary records. These were minted by `anchor_cas_hydrate_records` to satisfy **Rule B1**, which requires a registry `exactMatch` row for an *asymmetric* subject. #245 / PR #342 then moved exactly these records `narrowMatch → closeMatch`, on the grounds that ChEBI files hydrates under `CHEBI:35505` and never under the anhydrous parent. `closeMatch` is symmetric, so the B1 obligation lapsed and the builder correctly stops minting them. **Confirmed: 0 of the 67 carry an asymmetric row in either artifact.** Each keeps its `cas:` identity row and its CHEBI row, and `cas_rn` is in kg-microbe's `best_primary` chain.

**14 of the 20 added rows are the same rule working correctly** — 13 have a live `narrowMatch` so B1 requires the registry row; `Synthetic_Sea_Salts` holds its `kgmicrobe.compound` CURIE as its actual identifier.

Checked the 67 against kg-microbe's **2026-08-05** merged build, which carries 140 `kgmicrobe.compound:` nodes — so the namespace is live there — and **0 of the 67** and 0 of the 14 appear. kg-microbe materialises nodes for a record's identifier, not for synthesized SSSOM objects.

## The guard rewrite

`test_published_mim_subject_case.py` pinned the 64 case spellings as a literal table pending #236. It now pins **what those spellings stood for — that no published CURIE dangles** — across all 2,512 subjects instead of 64, and does not need rewriting every time a filename legitimately changes. The 64 stay as a regression cohort asserting *both* spellings still resolve.

Verified the guard fails as well as passes: dropping one alias row fails 2 tests.

## Verified on the promoted file

- `validate_sssom_invariants`: Rules **A, B1, B2, B3, C pass** (B4 skipped — no local kg-microbe transforms, the documented limitation)
- **0** subjects violate `_CURIE_RE` (was 11)
- **0** subjects lack a matching record file (was 82)
- header stamped `2026-08-21`
- **1042** tests pass

## Not in scope

#390 (142 `narrowMatch` rows inverted vs SKOS) rides along unchanged — kg-microbe's consolidator treats both asymmetric predicates identically, so the rows land correctly; flipping needs coordination. #301's in-place writers still don't stamp the header.

items.title: Settle the builder/published disagreement (#409), plus #406, #407, #410
items.body:
Four issues. The substantial one is **#409**, and it has a better answer than the question assumed.

## #409 — neither artifact is authoritative, wholesale

The 249-predicate disagreement decomposes into **two separate defects pointing opposite ways**:

| | rows | who is wrong | where fixed |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `exactMatch → closeMatch` | 227 | the **builder** | culturebotai-claw#74 |
| `closeMatch → exactMatch` | 22 | this **published file** | here |

**The 227.** Every one had `mapping_quality: SYNONYM_MATCH`, and the builder demoted anything not `EXACT_MATCH` to `closeMatch`. MIM's schema keeps them apart — `SYNONYM_MATCH` = "matches known synonym in ontology" (*how it was found*), `CLOSE_MATCH` = "semantically close but not exact". The demoted rows show it plainly: `nitrous oxide` → `dinitrogen oxide`, `Escin` → `Aescin`, `Disodium oxalate` → `sodium oxalate`.

**The 22.** Registry identity rows like `MIM:Terpene_hydrate → cas:2451-01-6`, where the object CURIE **is** that record's own identifier and the object label repeats the subject label. Identity by construction, published as `closeMatch`.

**Predicate flips between the two artifacts: 249 → 0.** SSSOM Rules A/B1/B2/B3/C still pass.

### The first cut of that script was wrong, and the check caught it

It promoted **353** rows, not 22. Matching on "object == identifier" also catches every ordinary record's *primary mapping* row — for a normally-mapped record the identifier **is** the ontology term — and the builder agrees `closeMatch` on 273 of those because a curator graded them `CLOSE_MATCH`. Promoting them would have overwritten curation decisions. It now additionally requires the record's identifier to **differ** from its ontology parent, which is the builder's own dual-emission condition.

## #406 — the check disagreed with itself

`check_instruction_refs` already had `tracked_paths()`, whose docstring says a filesystem check "answers differently on a developer machine than in CI". It applied that to the *targets* of references but not to *which files it scans*, so an untracked scratch file was checked locally and invisible in CI. Verified: **34 filesystem matches, 33 tracked**.

## #407 — 71 duplicate nodes

`id` is the record identifier, and a merge tombstone deliberately carries the **winner's** identifier — so one node per record drew 60 identifiers 2–3 times in both artifacts. Deduped, tombstones losing to live records: **2,345 → 2,274 nodes, 0 duplicated ids**, and the #405 membership gate still passes.

The warning it prints is deliberately understated. This function **cannot** distinguish one record drawn twice from two live records sharing a CURIE, because the caller indexes by identifier and both nodes come back identical. Claiming otherwise would assert more than the evidence in hand.

## The bigger thing #407 uncovered — filed as #414

**30 ontology CURIEs are held by two or more LIVE records**, which MIM's own rule forbids (the identifier *is* the CURIE). They split two ways and need opposite fixes: genuine duplicates to merge (`Bacto peptone`/`Peptone`; `CaCl2` 502 occ /`Calcium Chloride` 15 occ), and **distinct substances wrongly sharing an identifier** that must *not* be merged (`CaSO4` vs `CaSO4 x 7 H2O`; `Citric acid` vs `Citric Acid•H2O`). Too large for this PR; filed with the enumeration.

## #410 — documented rather than changed

`CAS:<rn>` in `other` is a **display string, not a CURIE**. `other` is a free-text synonym column, so expanding any entry against the curie_map is a misreading regardless of case — and lowercasing to `cas:` would make it *look* expandable, the opposite of the intent. Recorded in `MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md`.

## Verified

- predicate flips 249 → 0; SSSOM invariants pass
- both graph artifacts: 0 duplicated ids; visualization membership gate green
- instruction-ref check: untracked file excluded (34 → 33)
- **947 tests pass, unchanged from the base commit** (confirmed by collecting on the stashed tree)

items.title: SSSOM delivery: document downstream predicate semantics, drop the one inverted row
items.body:
Prep for delivering the SSSOM to kg-microbe. Files #390 and #391; does not close #322/#317, which it reprioritises.

## kg-microbe's guidance changes what a predicate means for MIM

kg-microbe now consumes this file as the **authoritative** ingredient-mapping source (priority 11), synced straight from this repo as a sibling checkout — vendored copy is a cache, sibling always wins, a missing sibling is *fatal* to their consolidator. Nothing is required of MIM beyond merging to `main`.

The part MIM had not recorded:

> symmetric matches (`skos:exactMatch`, `skos:closeMatch`) **overwrite the canonical name** with MIM's `subject_label`; asymmetric (`narrowMatch`/`broadMatch`) keep the ontology label canonical and add the MIM term as a synonym.

| predicate | effect on the ontology term in the KG |
|---|---|
| `exactMatch` / `closeMatch` | **renamed** to MIM's `subject_label` |
| `narrowMatch` / `broadMatch` | label kept; MIM term added as synonym + parent edge |

**2,805 of 2,947 rows are symmetric, and 834 carry a label differing from the ontology's — so 834 rows rename a node in the knowledge graph.** That is deliberate (a recipe says `KOH`, not "potassium hydroxide", and MIM is the naming authority), but it makes `preferred_term` quality load-bearing in a way it was not before.

**It also reprioritises #322 and #317.** Over-grading is no longer a private inaccuracy: a record graded `EXACT_MATCH` against a class term both asserts a false identity *and renames the class*. 118 `exactMatch` rows currently target CHEBI terms with no formula.

`MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` previously described `subject_label` only as "how downstream consumers resolve raw strings". It now documents the renaming consequence.

## The one row that lands backwards

`Aromatic hydrocarbon` was the corpus's **only** `skos:broadMatch` row. MIM defines broadMatch as *"MIM:X is broader than Y"*; kg-microbe reads narrowMatch and broadMatch **identically** as *"the MIM subject is a NARROWER concept than the object"*, so it published this record as a **child** of `polycyclic arene` — backwards, and chemically false.

The record contradicted itself:

```
REGRADED_CLASS_OVERSTATEMENT  EXACT_MATCH -> BROAD_MATCH (#322)
                              "the record is BROADER than the term"
MINTED_REGISTRY_IDENTIFIER    CHEBI:33848 -> kgmicrobe.compound:...
                              "The record is narrower than CHEBI:33848"
```

The regrade was right; the mint applied §3 step 3's boilerplate rationale without re-reading it.

**Fixed by §3 step 1, not a predicate flip.** `CHEBI:33658 "arene"` is defined as *"Any monocyclic or polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon"* — exactly what the record names, and never looked for. Grounding there makes the mapping symmetric and true, so the direction question disappears, and it retires a mint the record never needed. Not a #322 overstatement: both sides are the same class. 0 occurrences.

The replacement row is written by the script reusing the **existing** `MIM:` subject rather than re-deriving it from the label (#293/#307) — `reconcile_sssom` correctly refuses to invent provenance for a new row.

## Recorded, deliberately not changed — #390

MIM's `narrowMatch` is **inverted relative to SKOS**: the spec makes it a sub-property of `skos:narrower`, so `A narrowMatch B` asserts B is *narrower* than A, while this repo uses it for "MIM:X is a kind-of Y". 141 rows.

Nothing is broken today, because kg-microbe reads MIM's intent rather than the spec. **Flipping them unilaterally would invert 141 subclass edges downstream**, so it needs a coordinated change on both sides. Filed rather than fixed.

Also filed **#391**: two cow-manure records with opposite grades, one holding an ENVO id it simultaneously grades `BROAD_MATCH` against.

## Verification

- **0 `skos:broadMatch` rows remain**
- `reconcile_sssom` in sync; invariants pass Rules A, B1, B2, B3, C
- `validate-all` 0 errors, `validate_strict` 0 ERROR rows, filename case clean
- **931 tests pass**

items.title: Three small fixes: index generator wiring, MICRO object_source, the `X` mapping (#380, #381, #356)
items.body:
Closes #380, closes #381. Advances #356 without closing it.

Three independent fixes that needed no decisions.

## #380 — nine published artifacts nobody regenerated

`generate_index_files.py` writes `{mapped,unmapped,all}_ingredients_index.{csv,json}` plus the three `.md` digests under `data/curated/`, and was reachable from **no recipe and no CI job**. It had already gone stale, still advertising `UNMAPPED_0434 | Marine broth 2216` after that record was promoted to a mint.

A recipe alone does not fix this — #217 added one for `export-lists` and the same defect turned up here anyway — so the load-bearing part is the **CI assertion that regenerating is a no-op**. I verified the generator is idempotent and writes no timestamps *before* wiring it: a gate that goes red on every run gets deleted rather than obeyed.

Added `just export-indexes`, folded into `build-docs`.

## #381 — MICRO promotions published an empty `object_source`

`OBJECT_SOURCE` had no `MICRO` key and the lookup is `.get(prefix, "")`, so a MICRO promotion emitted a **blank column silently**, alongside the 51 correct `obo:micro.owl` rows already in the file.

Added `MICRO` and `BTO` — both **verified against the rows actually published**, not assumed (`obo:micro.owl` ×51, `obo:bto.owl` ×1) — and removed the local override `add_culturemech_gap_labels.py` was carrying, so there is one table again. Every `object_source` value in use is now covered.

**Added Rule C** to `validate_sssom_invariants.py`: no published row may have an empty `object_source`. This is the part that prevents recurrence — the failure is silent by construction, so the table cannot be trusted to stay complete on its own. Verified it bites: blanking one cell gives `rc=2`, `Rule C: 1`.

## #356 — `X` was mapped to the 24th letter of the alphabet

`NCIT:C189218`'s OLS definition, in full:

> The 24th letter of the English alphabet.

The record carried it at `EXACT_MATCH` across **101 occurrences**. The grade was not wrong about the *string* — a name-normalisation pass matched label to term label — but nothing in that path checked the result was a substance.

**What `X` denotes is still unknown, and this PR does not guess.** That needs source archaeology in the CultureBot media, which is why #356 stays open. But the mapping should not stand meanwhile: the record returns to `UNMAPPED_0818`, which is honest and strictly better than publishing a letter of the alphabet as an ingredient. Moved into `unmapped_ingredients.yaml` (#370), SSSOM row dropped, former mapping preserved in `curation_history`.

### The suggested guard was run, and is deliberately not wired into CI

#356 proposed flagging any `EXACT_MATCH` whose label is ≤3 characters and whose target has no formula/SMILES/InChI/CAS. Over the corpus it returns four:

| label | target | occ | verdict |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `X` | NCIT:C189218 "X" | 101 | **wrong** — the letter |
| `Rna` | mesh:D012313 "RNA" | 0 | correct — a polymer has no single formula |
| `Pea` | NCIT:C72056 "Pea" | 2 | plausible; NCIT leaves it undefined |
| `Fig` | NCIT:C71971 "Fig" | 0 | plausible; likewise |

One true positive in four. Excellent as a one-off sweep, poor as a permanent gate — the absent-chemistry signal fires on every legitimate polymer and food term, and a check that cries wolf three times in four gets switched off. Recorded in the script's docstring instead.

## Verification

- `validate-all` 0 errors / 0 warnings; `validate_strict` 0 ERROR rows
- `validate_sssom_invariants` — passes Rules A, B1, B2, B3, **C**
- `reconcile_sssom` — 0 GAP / 0 ORPHAN / 0 STALE
- round trip closed; filename case clean
- **931 tests pass**
- `X` no longer resolves to `NCIT:C189218` in `label_index.csv` or the SSSOM; it resolves to `UNMAPPED_0818`

items.title: Settle hydrate identity and unscramble hydrate CAS numbers (#225, #334)
items.body:
Closes #225, closes #334.

## Most of both issues was already done — verified, not assumed

**All five of #225's claimed collisions are resolved**, each onto the correct term:

| folded name | #225 said | now |
|---|---|---|
| `MgSO4·7H2O` / `MgSO47H2O` | CHEBI:32599 **and** CHEBI:31795 | **CHEBI:31795** (heptahydrate) |
| `FeSO4 x 7 H2O` | CHEBI:75836 **and** CHEBI:75832 | **CHEBI:75836** (heptahydrate) |
| `MgCl2 x 6 H2O` | CHEBI:86345 **and** CHEBI:6636 | **CHEBI:86345** (hexahydrate) |
| `Glucose` / `Maltose` | two ids each | one each |

**#334's two merges are done too** — `CoCl2 x 6 H2O` and `NiCl2 x 6 H2O` are REJECTED against the representatives holding CHEBI:53503 / CHEBI:53542, which is exactly the merge it asked for.

What remained: the two promotions, and the CAS half.

## Promotions

`Na2HPO4 x 2 H2O` and `x 12 H2O` were **already grounded** to CHEBI:91258 / CHEBI:91259 — the exact dihydrate and dodecahydrate terms — while keeping a registry mint and `CLOSE_MATCH`. They *are* those substances.

The identifier and the grade move together because the corpus says so: **all 54 registry-identified records are graded non-exact**, so a mint means "not the term". Now `identifier == ontology_id` at `EXACT_MATCH`, matching `MgSO4 x 7 H2O`.

**Rule D (#438) caught the consequence** — the published identity rows were still `closeMatch` to what is now the record's own identifier. Flipped to `exactMatch`, and the two registry rows pointing at the retired mints dropped, since claw's builder emits that row only when `primary_id != obj_id`.

## CAS — the general check found far more than #334's list

| | |
|---|---|
| fixed from ChEBI's dbxref on the hydrate-specific term | **6** |
| dropped (hydrate carrying its anhydrous parent's CAS, no ChEBI term) | **20** |

Two were from #334's list; the other four (`FeSO4 x 7H2O`, `MnSO4 x 1 H2O`, `CoSO4 x 7 H2O`, `(NH4)2Ni(SO4)2 x 6 H2O`) came from stating the check in general form.

**Dropped rather than replaced.** There is no authoritative value for those hydration states, and substituting a guess is how wrong CAS numbers spread — absent is recoverable, wrong is not. The grounding is separately wrong for most of them (#321); this corrects only the CAS.

Why it mattered, in #334's own words: `7791-20-0` sat on the di- and pentahydrate while belonging to the hexahydrate, so **a CAS-keyed join run then would have merged the wrong records**.

### How the corpus test is phrased, and why

Stated as *"no hydrate carries its own anhydrous parent's CAS"* — not *"no two hydration states share a CAS"*. The looser form also fires on records whose CAS faithfully reflects a wrong **grounding**, which is #321's defect; a test conflating the two cannot be satisfied by fixing either.

## Two guards fired and were right

- **Rule D** on the identity rows, above.
- **`test_symmetric_rows_carry_their_records_cas`** (#403) — the SSSOM `other` column publishes the record's CAS as a KGX synonym, and two rows still held the old value. Remedy re-run as the test instructs.

## Gates

| | |
|---|---|
| SSSOM | Rules A, B1, B2, B3, C, D, E |
| `validate-strict` | 0 errors / 2853 files |
| `qc-roundtrip` | verified |
| `qc-duplicate-ids` | matches baseline |
| export freshness | 8/8 |
| pytest | **1337 passed**, 1 skipped |

## Known consequence, accepted deliberately

The promotion strands **463 membership edges** — CultureMech resolves against a pinned MIM index, so its edges keep the old `kgmicrobe.compound:` ids until it re-resolves. Membership rebuilt: 192,079 → 191,616, with both retired ids in `reports/culturemech_membership_unknown_ids.tsv` (304 and 159 recipes). The gap is **visible rather than silent**, which is what the report added in #498 is for.

---

## Adversarial review of this PR

| Finding | Filed | In this PR? |
|---|---|---|
| Removing a wrong CAS from a record did not stop the SSSOM publishing it | #501 | **Yes — closed** |

**#501 made the CAS half of this PR cosmetic.** Removing 20 wrong CAS numbers from the records left **32 SSSOM rows still carrying the exact values** in `other` — which per #403 become synonyms on the ontology entity in kg-microbe and from there KGX. The wrong numbers were still reaching the graph.

The guard only ever checked one direction: that a record's CAS *reaches* `other`. Adding was covered. Correcting was covered, because the old value fails the equality check — that is what caught two rows earlier here. **Removing was not**, because the row is then skipped as "no CAS on record", and removal is exactly the case where the published value is most likely wrong rather than merely stale.

34 orphaned tokens stripped; bidirectional guard added.

### My first attempt at that fix was wrong

It read `chemical_properties.cas_rn`, while the codebase's `_cas_for` prefers `supplied_form.cas_rn` — the number a lab actually orders by. That destroyed `D-lyxose`'s legitimate `CAS:1114-34-7`, which sits on its supplied form and is correctly published even though the denoted form carries none. Caught by checking my own strip against `_cas_for` before committing. Redone, and the new test **reuses** `_cas_for` rather than reimplementing it so the two cannot diverge.

## Three existing guards fired, all correctly

This PR is a good advertisement for the repo's invariants — each caught a real downstream consequence I had not anticipated:

1. **Rule D (#438)** — identity rows still `closeMatch` to what had become the record's own identifier.
2. **`test_symmetric_rows_carry_their_records_cas` (#403)** — two rows holding a superseded CAS.
3. **`check_visualization_currency`** — `ingredient_umap.json` and `ingredient_graph.json` named 2 retired identities. Regenerated; wrong identities 2 → 0.

## Verified, not assumed

- **The dropped CAS values remain recoverable**: every one is recorded in its record's curation history with the reason, so "absent is recoverable, wrong is not" is literally true here.
- **A pre-existing orphan surfaced** while writing the reverse check — `D-lyxose` — which is how I discovered the `supplied_form` semantics rather than shipping the wrong strip.

## Worktree note

`data/embeddings/` holds untracked symlinks into MicroGrowLink, so a fresh worktree has none and `just generate-visualizations` fails on a missing path. Pass `--embeddings-path` explicitly.

items.title: Triage the CultureMech unresolved residual, and land its alias head
items.body:
## What this is

CultureMech has 6,105 ingredient mentions (1,911 distinct labels) that MIM cannot
resolve. Read raw, that looks like ~1,900 compounds needing research. It isn't, and the
first commit is the triage that shows why: CultureMech resolves against MIM's **literal**
label index, so a surface form differing only by a vendor tag, a concentration, or a
middot codepoint fails even where MIM already holds the compound.

| bucket | labels | mentions | meaning |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| ALIAS | 274 | 935 | folds onto a MAPPED record -- spelling only |
| UNMAPPED | 210 | 1,116 | folds onto a record that exists but is ungrounded |
| AMBIGUOUS | 55 | 383 | two or more records publish the label (#504) |
| NOISE | 24 | 618 | CultureMech parse damage (CultureMech#387) |
| RESIDUAL | 1,348 | 3,053 | genuinely absent -- the real grounding work |

42% of the unresolved mass needed no grounding at all.

## What it lands

- **276 surface forms added as synonyms** on the 156 records that already denote them.
  Asserts no new chemical identity.
- **4 records promoted to MICRO** on exact synonym matches: `BG-11 Medium` ->
  MICRO:0001348, `Bordet-Gengou-Agar-Base` -> MICRO:0002398, `Casman-Agar-Base` ->
  MICRO:0002402, `Ox-bile` -> MICRO:0000610.
- **Measured effect: 287 more labels (940 recipe mentions) resolve literally.** Index
  8,367 -> 9,394 rows, all new rows `unique`, conflict count unchanged at 468, nothing
  removed.

Four tools, all dry-run or read-only by default: `triage_culturemech_residual.py`,
`apply_culturemech_aliases.py`, `propose_residual_groundings.py`,
`create_records_from_groundings.py`.

It also unblocks MICRO in `promote_resolved_unmapped.py`. MICRO models named growth
media, MIM publishes 48 MICRO records, and OBJECT_SOURCE has carried `obo:micro.owl`
since #381 -- but the guard was keyed on ONTOLOGY_DB and MICRO's local build is a 0-byte
stub, so every MICRO promotion was refused. `canonical_label` now falls back to OLS4,
looking a term up by `obo_id` rather than a constructed IRI (MICRO:0002398's IRI is
`.../obo/MicrO.owl/MICRO_0002398`, so the constructed form 404s on exactly the terms this
unblocks), rejecting obsolete terms and IRI-fragment labels.

## The part worth reviewing closely

**Five defects, every one found by auditing output rather than reading code.** Each would
have shipped a wrong identity or an unreviewable diff.

1. **The fold discarded chemistry.** Under `re.IGNORECASE` the vendor-tag branch matched
   *any* parenthetical: `AlK(SO4)2 (anhydrous)` folded to `alk 2`, `EDTA(Disodium salt)`
   to `edta`. And hydration state is identity -- CaCl2 and CaCl2 x 2 H2O are 110.98 and
   147.01 g/mol (MAPPING_SEMANTICS Section 3) -- so folding `(anhydrous)` away lets an
   anhydrous form inherit a hydrate's identifier. **A wrong mapping where the status quo
   was merely a missing one.** Fixing it moved 70 labels out of ALIAS.
2. **NCIT captured everything.** 2.7 GB of clinical and gene concepts whose *alias* space
   collides with ingredient names: `B12` -> `TNFAIP1 wt Allele`, `Absolute ethanol` ->
   `Alcohol`, plus `Potato`/`Skim milk` that belong in FOODON. NCIT and MESH are now
   label-only and last in preference order.
3. **Every OLS4 synonym match was silently discarded**, because a server-side exact match
   was re-checked client-side against the label alone. `Christensen's urea agar` -- an
   exact MICRO synonym of `urea agar` -- was thrown away. The MICRO pass was label-only
   without reporting it.
4. **Ontology preference was decided by capitalisation.** oaklib's `basic_search` is
   case-sensitive, so with query variants as the outer loop the raw `Air` reached NCIT
   before the normalised `air` reached ENVO: the same substance grounded to NCIT:C73434
   and ENVO:00002005.
5. **`width=100` on the YAML dump** reflowed every long string, burying 2 added lines
   under 33 spurious ones. The corpus canonical format is PyYAML's default wrap
   (verified: 60/60 sampled records round-trip byte-identically without it).
6. **An exact match does not mean the term is a substance.** `Dissolve` matched
   NCIT:C64929 (a procedure) and `Stock A` matched NCIT:C14643 -- perfect label matches,
   neither an ingredient. This is the #356 class, where `X` was published as EXACT_MATCH
   against the 24th letter of the alphabet on a record with 101 occurrences, and no
   amount of ontology routing fixes it because the string really does match. Terms from
   broad ontologies must now descend from NCIT:C1908.
7. **I routed around a guard without recognising it as one.** The OLS4 fallback looks
   terms up by `obo_id` *because* MicrO's IRI is malformed -- which is exactly the
   condition `MICRO_VERIFIED` gates on. CI caught it: two promotions were demoted, and
   the fallback now refuses `is_defining_ontology=false` itself (requesting `fieldList`
   explicitly, since OLS4 omits the field unless asked and the check would read None and
   silently pass).

Guards, each added after it caught something real: `REJECTED_LABEL` never promoted
(#477); an identifier held by >1 record skipped (ownership is a merge decision); a
spelling two records would claim dropped (an ambiguous index row is worse than a miss --
CultureMech fails closed on it); case variants collapsed; names under 3 characters never
matched (`X` hit UBERON's "area X of ventral lateral nucleus").

No `occurrence_count` on synonyms: none of the corpus's ~7k carries one, and MIM's counts
are over MIM's ingest while these are over CultureMech's -- mixing them double-counts,
per the rule set in `add_culturemech_gap_labels.py`.

## What it deliberately does not do

- **Does not resolve the 55 ambiguous labels** (#504). Three defects are mixed there, and
  one is an identity error published *now*: `CoCl2 6H2O` matches records for the di- and
